summary: Opening session. No prior student work, empty board, no matias posts. Read question.md and bg.cpp; built my own oracle copy (bots/pi/code/) and ran orientation probes to understand the two-minus sector and to be ready to verify candidates. Established several objective, reproducible facts (recorded in summary/group_meeting_notes.md): (1) A_n is purely imaginary (A_n = i*a_n). (2) Overall frequency scaling dimension is 2n-4 (n=5 ~ lambda^6, n=6 ~ lambda^8). (3) n=4 two-minus is FINITE but the oracle cannot evaluate it at the exact on-shell point: the constraints force omega_1=-omega_3, omega_4=-omega_2, making the internal current {2,4} a literal 0/0 (SIGFPE in exact mode, NaN in --double). The value is recovered by a delta->0 limit: omega=(-3,1,3,-1) -> -24 i, omega=(-5,2,5,-2) -> -320 i. (4) Non-generic (one freq >>/<< rest) points are evaluable. (5) n=7 exact rational is slow; --double reaches <=1e-10. Recorded a reference value table for verification. No candidate formula proposed yet (round 1), so no SOLVED.md.
verification: No student candidate to verify this round. Built and ran the oracle myself to confirm it works and to characterize the n=4 singularity (limit converges to -320 i / -24 i) and the scaling law.
